Sec. 4-174

(a) Definitions.

The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them
in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Livestock means any cow, horse, sheep, goat, or other similar animal commonly found ona farm.

Therapeutic facility means an appropriately licensed/certified facility which exists primarily for the diagnosis,
and treatment of mental, physical, or emotional medical conditions.

At large animal means an animal that is not confined to the premises of the owner, within a house, fence, or
other structure, or restrained by a leash sufficiently strong enough to prevent the animal from escaping and
restricting the animal to the premises.

Fence means a physical barrier cdnstructed out of such a material as to provide a barrier between the animal
and the public. This fencing must not be of a material that requires electricity from batteries to operate.

(b) Authorization to keep livestock.

(1) Notwithstanding any city ordinances in conflict in whole or in part with any provision of this section an
approved therapeutic facility is hereby authorized to acquire, keep, and house within the city limits any
and all livestock or animals described within this article and deemed necessary and suitable for a
therapeutic purpose, program, service, or other activity. Said purpose, program, service, or other
activity must have as its primary goal and objective the therapeutic treatment, education, or diagnosis of
individuals of any age with special needs, developmental delays, or other similar condition.

(2) In order to be considered an approved therapeutic facility and to receive the authorization to keep
livestock as referenced herein, the therapeutic facility must submit the following to the City’s Public
Works Director: the facility's license, certification, and/or accreditation, as appropriate, to conduct the
therapeutic treatment that it intends to offer; the nature of the therapeutic treatment that it intends to
offer; a detailed list of the livestock and other similar animals that the facility intends to keep and the
location it intends to keep them; the facility’s detailed plan for how it intends to safely and humanely
house, feed, and care for said animals; and any other relevant information requested by the Public
Works Director. The Public Works Director, upon consultation with the City’s Animal Services Director,
shall consider the information presented, as well as how the facility may affect the surrounding area,
businesses, and residents, and then approve or deny the requested authorization. A denial of
authorization may be appealed to the Cabot Planning Commission within 30 calendar days of the denial
and according to the procedures laid out elsewhere in the Code of Cabot for appeals to the Planning

Commission.

(c) Locations authorized.

The authorization for any approved therapeutic facility to keep livestock and other similar animals as
discussed herein is limited to the approved location referenced herein in subsection (b).

(d) Inspections.

The city animal services department shall be permitted to enter into an approved therapeutic facility and
associated grounds in order to perform routine inspections of any animal establishment, animals on premises, and
the grounds where such animals are kept at any reasonable time during normal business hours to ensure
compliance with all provisions of City code regarding animals.

(e) Medical requirements.

All animals on premises shall be current on all vaccinations and veterinary requirements. Records of
vaccinations and treatments shall be kept on site and available for inspections by city animal services department
or other appropriate authority.

(f) Animal restraint.

All animals must be leashed or secured by harness when not in designated kennel areas; this applies even
within fenced areas. All kennels and stalls must be located within a properly fenced area. All animals restrained by
leash, lead, rope or similar restraint must be controlled by persons with the physical capability of handling such
animal.

(g) Minimum care.

(1) Shelter.

(a)All animals shall have continuous access to a structurally sound, moisture proof and windproof shelter,
large enough to keep the animals reasonably clean and dry.

(b)A shelter which does not protect the animal from temperature extremes or precipitation, or which
does not provide adequate ventilation or drainage, is not sufficient and does not comply with this
section.

(c) The animal's shelter and bedding and other accessible space shall be maintained in a manner which
minimizes the risk of the animal contracting disease, being injured or becoming infested with parasites.

(2) Nutrition.

(a)It shall be unlawful for any person keeping or harboring any animal to fail, refuse or neglect to provide
such an animal with clean, fresh, potable water adequate for the animal's size, age, and physical
condition. This water supply shall either be free flowing or provided in a removable receptacle that is
weighted or secured to prevent tipping.

(b)It shall be unlawful for any person keeping or harboring any animal to fail, refuse or neglect to provide
such animal with wholesome foodstuff suitable for the animal, animal's physical condition and age, and
in significant quantities to maintain an adequate level of nutrition for the animal.

(3) Exercise. The enclosure of the confinement area for the animal shall encompass sufficient usable space to
keep the animal in good condition.
(h)Standards for animal establishments.

All animal establishments, including animal establishments in conjunction with another holding facility, shall,
in addition to other requirements, comply with the minimum standards of this section.

(1) The following animals are considered to be public nuisances and are in violation of this section:

(b)Any animal that is offensive or dangerous to the public health, safety or welfare by virtue of the

(2)All stables used for housing livestock which violate any of these provisions of city law, are hereby declared

expense provide adequate enclosures, structures and approved waste disposal activities, and all other supporting
facilities, labor, and sites required as necessary to carry out the educational, therapeutic or diagnostic purposes

described herein.

(k) Penalties.

In addition to any other penalties provided under City code, an individual or therapeutic facility that violates

of its approval and authorization to acquire, keep, and house livestock and related animals within city limits.

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND ARTICLE IV SECTION 4.11 OF THE
UNIFIED DEVELOPMENT CODE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, it is the desire of the Cabot City Council to amend Article IV of the
Unified Development Code (“UDC”) Section 4.11 to further economic development and
support new small businesses; and

WHEREAS, state law empowers municipalities to adopt ordinances to provide
for the safety, health, comfort, and convenience of inhabitants of the city; therefore, the
purpose for these amendments is to carry out and protect various elements of the
Comprehensive Development Plan and all other adopted plans and policies of the City of
Cabot and to promote the safety, order, convenience, prosperity, and general welfare of

4.11.1 Purpose and General Provisions

The purpose of this section is to establish requirements, limitations, and exceptions for the
continued existence of uses, lots, and structures that are deemed to not conform with this Code.
Such nonconformities may continue, but the provisions of this Section are designed to curtail
their enlargement or expansion and encourage their eventual elimination in order to preserve the
integrity of the Zoning Districts and the requirements established by these regulations.

A structure, use of land, a use of a structure, or lot of record may be made non-conforming in the
following ways:

a. It was legally established prior to the effective date of the original adoption of this Code.

b. It was legally established prior to the effective date of an amendment of this Code that made
it non-conforming.

c. It was annexed into the City of Cabot and did not conform to this Code at the time of
annexation. Such structures, uses of land, and uses of a structure are considered legally
established. Annexed lots of record shall not be considered legally established unless within a
platted subdivision that bears a certificate of final plat approval by the Cabot Planning
Commission and which is officially filed with the Pulaski or Lonoke County Recorder.

AN ORDINANCE TO REZONE 1901 SOUTH PINE STREET, CITY OF CABOT,
FROM R-1, SINGLE-FAMILY TO C-2, GENERAL COMMERCIAL; AMENDING THE
LAND USE PLAN; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission is empowered to regulate and control the
development of land within the planning jurisdiction of the City of Cabot pursuant to Ark. Code Ann.
§14-56-417; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission held its regularly scheduled meeting on April
23, 2024, and approved the request of Austin Godwin, to rezone a parcel of land as follows,

1901 South Pine Street

from R-1, Single-Family Residential District to C-2, General Commercial District, more specifically
set forth in the legal description attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by this
reference and referring the same to this governing body for approval; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot Planning Commission further approved an amendment to the City’s
Land Use Plan to reflect consistency with the change in use; referring the same to this body for
approval.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: A tract of land known as 1901 South Pine Street, Cabot, Lonoke County,
Arkansas, more specifically set forth in the legal description attached hereto as Exhibit A and
incorporated herein by this reference, is hereby rezoned from R-1 to C-2.

SECTION 2: The City’s Land Use Plan is hereby amended to incorporate the change in the

land use as stated above.

The City of Cabot (Applicant) hereby assures and certifies to the Arkansas Economic Development
Commission regarding an application for Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds, the
following:

THRESHOLD CERTIFICATIONS
1. There are no significant unresolved audit findings relating to any prior grant award from the federal
 and/or state government that would adversely affect the administration of this grant.

2. No legal actions are underway or being contemplated that would significantly impact the Applicant’s
 capacity to effectively administer the program, and to fulfill the CDBG program; and

3. No project costs have been incurred that have not been approved in writing by the Commission.

FEDERAL COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATIONS
4. It will adopt and follow a residential anti-displacement and relocation assistance plan that will
 minimize displacement as a result of activities assisted with CDBG funds.

5. It will conduct and administer its programs in conformance with:
 a. Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Pub. L. 88-352), and the regulations issued pursuant
 thereto (24 CFR Part 1).

 b. Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1968 (Pub. L. 90-284), as amended, administering all programs
 and activities relating to housing and community development in a manner to affirmatively
 further fair housing, and will take action to affirmatively further fair housing in the sale or rental
 of housing, the financing of housing and the provision of brokerage services.

 c. The Fair Housing Act of 1988 (42 USC 3601-20) and will affirmatively further fair housing.

6. It will not attempt to recover any capital costs of public improvements assisted in whole or part by
 assessing any amount against properties owned and occupied by persons of low- and moderate-
 income, including any fee charged or assessment made as a condition of obtaining access to such
 public improvements, unless (1) grant funds are used to pay the proportion of such fee or
 assessment that relates to the capital costs of such public improvements that are financed from
 revenue sources other than grant funds, or (2) for purposes of assessing any amount against
 properties owned and occupied by persons of LMI who are not persons of very-low income, the

 citizen's views and responding to proposals and questions. The hearings must cover community

ORDINANCE NO. 18 OF 2024

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE BOUNDARIES OF THE PREVIOUSLY
ESTABLISHED ARTS AND ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT FOR THE CITY OF
CABOT, ESTABLISHING THE RULES AND REGULATIONS THEREOF;
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, in Ordinance 20 of 2019 the Cabot City Council established the Cabot Arts
and Entertainment District and established the boundaries thereof; and

WHEREAS, in consideration of the economic development and growth in the intervening
years, the City Council desires to expand the boundary of the previously established Arts and
Entertainment District; and

WHEREAS, under state law it is the responsibility of the city to establish rules and
regulations for an established Arts and Entertainment District; and

WHEREAS, therefore the Cabot City Council herein amends the boundaries of the city’s
previously established Arts and Entertainment District and establishes rules and regulations of said
district as provided in state law.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The boundaries of the Arts and Entertainment District established by
Ordinance 20 of 2019 are hereby amended to reflect the attached Exhibit A, incorporated herein
by this reference.

SECTION 2: Rules and regulations for the Arts & Entertainment District are hereby
established consistent with the attached Exhibit B. The Cabot City Council has sole authority to
make substantive changes to the rules and regulations adopted in Exhibit B. The Mayor may make
administrative changes to said rules and regulations as may be needed to protect the health, safety,
and welfare of the people of Cabot

SECTION 3: Pursuant to state law, the Clerk~Treasurer shall, within ten days of the
passage of this Ordinance, provide notice of the same to the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division

of the Department of Finance and Administration.

SECTION 4: Any Ordinances and Resolutions, or parts of the same, in conflict with this
Ordinance are hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.

SECTION 5: The legislation adopted herein is in furtherance of economic development
and growth and will directly benefit the public welfare. In order that said benefit to the people and.
City of Cabot may begin to accrue as soon as possible an emergency is hereby declared and this

Ordinance shall take effect from and upon its passage.

Cabot Arts and Entertainment District Rules and Regulations

SECTION 1: The Cabot Arts and Entertainment District (the Entertainment District)
may only be utilized pursuant to these rules and regulations and with an approved permit as
provided for herein. The public consumption of alcoholic beverages or possession of open
containers of alcoholic beverages in public outdoor areas within the Entertainment District is
prohibited except when specifically authorized by a Cabot Entertainment District Special Event
Permit upon the approval of the Mayor or his designee, and shall be subject to the terms and
conditions of said permit. The Entertainment District Special Event Permit must be obtained by
any establishment or vendor desiring to sell or distribute alcoholic beverages for consumption or
possession in an outdoor public area.

An Entertainment District Special Event Permit issued by the Mayor or designee shall
authorize the outdoor consumption of alcohol in outdoor public area only in the approved
specified areas in the permit and only during the approved times specified in the permit.
Additional conditions may be placed on the permittee, the event, and any individual who wishes
to allow their patrons to participate in the event as part of the authorization at the discretion of

the Mayor or designee.

SECTION 2: Any establishment or vendor wishing to provide alcoholic beverages at an
outdoor event held within the District shall fill out the Entertainment District Special Event
Permit Application available on the City of Cabot website and available for pick up at Cabot City
Hall and shall follow the rules and procedures contained therein. Applications will not be
reviewed until the complete application and a $100 permit fee has been properly submitted.
Approved permits shall be revoked prior to the event if all conditions are not met or all rules and
procedures are not followed. The Mayor or designee reserves the right and maintains sole
discretion over the decision to cancel or postpone any approved event held in/on city property at

any time. Applications shall be considered in consecutive order of when they were submitted.

SECTION 3: In the application for an Entertainment District Special Events permit, the

applicant shall give specific details regarding the start and end time of the requested event, the

EXHIBIT

iB
--- page 10 (OCR) ---
expected number of patrons, the planned types of alcohol (beer, wine, liquor, etc.), as well as the
boundaries of the special event, and any other information requested by the Mayor or designee.
The Mayor or designee may also impose any other additional limitations and conditions on the
event as he or she may deem appropriate to maintain public health, safety, and welfare for the

specific event at issue, including, but not limited to, an insurance requirement.

SECTION 4: Any establishment or vendor that receives an Entertainment District
Special Event Permit may allow alcoholic beverages to be removed from the licensed premises
only in a disposable Entertainment District container that bears the City-approved logo and the
establishment name. The containers are not to exceed 16 fluid ounces in size and are to be
provided by each establishment. The container design and specifications must be pre-approved
by the Mayor or designee prior to the event as part of the permit process.

No person shall possess on or about the outdoor public areas located within the
Entertainment District any open alcoholic beverage container that exceeds 16 fluid ounces in
size.

It shall be unlawful for any permit holder to provide or any patron to drink or attempt to
drink any alcoholic beverage from a can, bottle, or glass container, or to possess any open can,
bottle, or glass container of alcoholic beverages on the streets, sidewalks, rights-of-way, and

parking lots located within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 5: Establishments or vendors shall also provide a unique (in color or design)
wristband to each patron that purchases or receives alcohol during a special event. The
wristband, unique to each establishment or vendor, designates that the permit holder has checked.
photo identification to determine that the patron is legally able to consume an alcoholic
beverage. The design and specifications of the wristband must be pre-approved by the Mayor or

designee prior to the event as part of the permit process.

SECTION 6: It shall be unlawful to create, possess, or distribute fraudulent or

unauthorized Entertainment District containers or wristbands.
--- page 11 (OCR) ---
SECTION 7: No permit holder shall provide a patron with more than one open
container of alcoholic beverage at a time, and it shall be unlawful for any person to exit such
licensed premises with more than one such Entertainment District container. No establishment

shall provide alcohol to a patron that appears to be intoxicated.

SECTION 8: All establishments with an Entertainment District special event permit
shall prominently display the rules of the Cabot Entertainment District and a map of the event
boundaries within the Entertainment District. The permit holder shall clearly mark event
boundaries with prominent signage, designating to patrons where they may not cross with

alcoholic beverages.

SECTION 9: No alcoholic beverages purchased outside of the Entertainment District

shall be allowed in open containers within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 10: No person shall be permitted to leave the boundaries of the event with an
open alcoholic beverage container or an Entertainment District cup. All unfinished quantities of
alcohol and all District cups must be properly disposed of prior to the individual leaving the
event boundaries. Any person found with an Entertainment District cup or open container of
alcohol outside the set boundaries is subject to seizure by law enforcement or any officer of the
Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage Commission and the container and its contents shall be seized and
destroyed. In addition, any person found with a District container who is not displaying a proper

wristband shall have their container seized and the contents destroyed.

The seizure and destruction of the alcohol and any citation issued may be in addition to
law enforcement exercising their legal authority to charge or arrest any person for minor in
possession, public intoxication, disorderly conduct, or any other law that may be relevant to the
actions of the person. In addition, any person with a District container and/or wristband is subject
to age verification by law enforcement and/or any officer of the Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage

Commission while in the Entertainment District.
--- page 12 (OCR) ---
SECTION iL: Consumption of alcohol in a motor vehicle is prohibited. It shall be
unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage while in the confines of a motor
vehicle that is located upon any public street, parking lot, or other place in which the public has

or is permitted to have access within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 12: All other Arkansas laws including, but not limited to, Ark. Code Ann. § 3-
3-201, et seq (prohibited practices regarding alcoholic beverages), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71- 207
(disorderly conduct), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71-212 (public intoxication), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71-

218 (consumption of alcohol in a motor vehicle) remain in effect and will be enforced.

SECTION 13: Nothing contained in this ordinance shall diminish the requirements or
authority of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division of the Department of Finance and

Administration concerning permits issued within the designated entertainment district.

SECTION 14: All Ordinances, Resolutions, or Orders of the City Council, or parts of

the same, in conflict with this Ordinance are repealed to the extent of such conflict.

SECTION 15: In addition to following all rules and regulations stated herein, a person
or entity seeking a permit hereunder must also comply with all federal laws, state laws, local
laws, and regulations and directives of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division of the

Department of Finance and Administration.

SECTION 16: A violation of any part of these rules and regulations constitutes an
unclassified misdemeanor and may be punishable by a fine of $1,000 and/or a up to 10 days in

jail.

ORDINANCE NO. 22 OF 2024

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE CODE OF CABOT; DECLARING AN
EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, there has been a recent increase in individuals camping or otherwise
sleeping on public property. The that the health, safety, and welfare of its citizens require the
regulation of camping and sleeping in public spaces; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council hereby finds that camping or otherwise sleeping on
public property is detrimental to the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of Cabot for each
of the following independent reasons: it can pose real and significant safety hazards to both
those sleeping/camping and to members of the general public, such hazards include but are not
limited to, unsanitary conditions, fire hazards, and environmental degradation; it can block or
otherwise impair the public’s access and use of roads, sidewalks, parks, and other public areas,
these problems are exacerbated when access to these areas are protected by state and federal law;
and it can have a negative effect on local businesses and business owners; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council finds that the City has a significant interest in
maintaining clean, safe, and accessible public spaces for all residents and visitors and it is the
intent of this legislation to ensure the same; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: The Code of Cabot is hereby amended to include the provisions as set
forth in Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: The Code changes enacted herein shall not apply to City-owned property
under the sole management and control of the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission, the
Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission, or other independent commission properly established
under state law unless and until said commission(s) choose to adopt these or similar provisions.
The City Council acknowledges that state law gives said commissions sole authority over the
matters regulated herein for property under their care.

SECTION 3: Any municipal legislation or portion of municipal legislation in conflict

with this Ordinance is hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.

WHEREAS, The City of Cabot and the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission seek to
help improve the recreation facilities and wishes to seek grant funding assistance; and

WHEREAS, in order to obtain the funds necessary to develop and/or improve the site for
such a recreation area, it is necessary to obtain an Outdoor Recreation Matching Grant from the
Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage and Tourism; and

WHEREAS, the plans for such recreation areas have been prepared and the price,
therefore, has been established; and

WHEREAS, this governing body understands the grantee and grantor will enter into a
binding agreement which obligates both parties to policies and procedures contained within the
Outdoor Recreation Matching Grant Application Guide, including, but not limited to the
following: the park area defined by the project boundary map, submitted with the application,
must remain in outdoor recreation use in perpetuity, regardless if the property is bought or
developed with matching grant funds and; all future overhead utility lines within the project
boundary must be placed underground and; the project area must remain open and available for
use by the public at all reasonable times of the day and year; facilities can be reserved for special
events, league play, etc. but cannot be reserved, leased or assigned for exclusive use, and; the
project area must be kept clean, maintained, and operated in a safe and healthful manner; and

WHEREAS, The Cabot City Council is well aware and apprised of the above-mentioned
project, and that the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission will provide the local portion of
the development cost of the entire project.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to make
application to the Arkansas Department of Parks, Heritage and Tourism for assistance to develop
recreational facilities for the City and the Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission. The Mayor
and City Clerk~Treasurer are further authorized to sign and complete any necessary documents
and take any further action necessary to effectuate the City’s participation in the grant referenced

herein.

Item #9 - Municipal Services - Code Of Cabot

Section 1. Definitions:
1.

"Public Property" means any public sidewalk, street, alleyway, right-of-way, or
City-owned property.

2.

"Campsite" means any place where bedding, sleeping bag, or other material used
for bedding purposes, or any stove or fire is placed, established, or maintained for
the purpose of maintaining a temporary place to live, whether or not such place
incorporates the use of any tent, lean-to, shack, or any other structure, or any
vehicle or part thereof.

3.

“Camp” means to set up or to remain in or at a camp-site.

Section 2. Sleeping or Camping on Public Property Prohibited:
1.

No person may sleep outdoors on public property at any time as a matter of
individual and public safety. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, cityowned structures and parts of structures that are not fully enclosed, such as the
Railyard Pavilion.

2.

No person may camp or occupy a campsite outdoors on public property as a
matter of individual and public safety. This prohibition includes, but is not
limited to, city-owned structures and parts of structures that are not fully
enclosed, such as the Railyard Pavilion.

3.

In addition to any other remedy provided by law, any person found in violation of
this section may be immediately removed from the premises. Such removal is
hereby deemed to be a legitimate governmental function for the purposes of the
Obstructing Governmental Operations statute under state law. Any person
removed from a campsite or other location where they are sleeping hereunder
must take all personal property with them. Personal property left behind shall be
considered abandoned and may be immediately disposed of by a member of the
Cabot Police Department or other City employee.

Section 3. Penalties:
1.

In addition to any other remedies listed herein, a violation of any of the
prohibitions of any section herein shall be considered a violation of the Code of
Cabot. Upon conviction, a violator shall be sentenced to a fine of up to $100.
Subsequent convictions shall be punished with a fine of up to $500.

Cabot Arts and Entertainment District Rules and Regulations

SECTION 1: The Cabot Arts and Entertainment District (the Entertainment District)
may only be utilized pursuant to these rules and regulations and with an approved permit as
provided for herein. The public consumption of alcoholic beverages or possession of open
containers of alcoholic beverages in public outdoor areas within the Entertainment District is
prohibited except when specifically authorized by a Cabot Entertainment District Special Event
Permit upon the approval of the Mayor or his designee, and shall be subject to the terms and
conditions of said permit. The Entertainment District Special Event Permit must be obtained by
any establishment or vendor desiring to sell or distribute alcoholic beverages for consumption or
possession in an outdoor public area.

An Entertainment District Special Event Permit issued by the Mayor or designee shall
authorize the outdoor consumption of alcohol in outdoor public area only in the approved
specified areas in the permit and only during the approved times specified in the permit.
Additional conditions may be placed on the permittee, the event, and any individual who wishes
to allow their patrons to participate in the event as part of the authorization at the discretion of

the Mayor or designee.

SECTION 2: Any establishment or vendor wishing to provide alcoholic beverages at an
outdoor event held within the District shall fill out the Entertainment District Special Event
Permit Application available on the City of Cabot website and available for pick up at Cabot City
Hall and shall follow the rules and procedures contained therein. Applications will not be
reviewed until the complete application and a $100 permit fee has been properly submitted.
Approved permits shall be revoked prior to the event if all conditions are not met or all rules and
procedures are not followed. The Mayor or designee reserves the right and maintains sole
discretion over the decision to cancel or postpone any approved event held in/on city property at

any time. Applications shall be considered in consecutive order of when they were submitted.

SECTION 3: In the application for an Entertainment District Special Events permit, the

applicant shall give specific details regarding the start and end time of the requested event, the
--- page 5 (OCR) ---
expected number of patrons, the planned types of alcohol (beer, wine, liquor, etc.), as well as the
boundaries of the special event, and any other information requested by the Mayor or designee.
The Mayor or designee may also impose any other additional limitations and conditions on the
event as he or she may deem appropriate to maintain public health, safety, and welfare for the

specific event at issue, including, but not limited to, an insurance requirement.

SECTION 4: Any establishment or vendor that receives an Entertainment District
Special Event Permit may allow alcoholic beverages to be removed from the licensed premises
only in a disposable Entertainment District container that bears the City-approved logo and the
establishment name. The containers are not to exceed 16 fluid ounces in size and are to be
provided by each establishment. The container design and specifications must be pre-approved
by the Mayor or designee prior to the event as part of the permit process.

No person shall possess on or about the outdoor public areas located within the
Entertainment District any open alcoholic beverage container that exceeds 16 fluid ounces in
size.

It shall be unlawful for any permit holder to provide or any patron to drink or attempt to
drink any alcoholic beverage from a can, bottle, or glass container, or to possess any open can,
bottle, or glass container of alcoholic beverages on the streets, sidewalks, rights-of-way, and

parking lots located within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 5: Establishments or vendors shall also provide a unique (in color or design)
wristband to each patron that purchases or receives alcohol during a special event. The
wristband, unique to each establishment or vendor, designates that the permit holder has checked.
photo identification to determine that the patron is legally able to consume an alcoholic
beverage. The design and specifications of the wristband must be pre-approved by the Mayor or

designee prior to the event as part of the permit process.

SECTION 6: It shall be unlawful to create, possess, or distribute fraudulent or

unauthorized Entertainment District containers or wristbands.
--- page 6 (OCR) ---
SECTION 7: No permit holder shall provide a patron with more than one open
container of alcoholic beverage at a time, and it shall be unlawful for any person to exit such
licensed premises with more than one such Entertainment District container. No establishment

shall provide alcohol to a patron that appears to be intoxicated.

SECTION 8: All establishments with an Entertainment District special event permit
shall prominently display the rules of the Cabot Entertainment District and a map of the event
boundaries within the Entertainment District. The permit holder shall clearly mark event
boundaries with prominent signage, designating to patrons where they may not cross with

alcoholic beverages.

SECTION 9: No alcoholic beverages purchased outside of the Entertainment District

shall be allowed in open containers within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 10: No person shall be permitted to leave the boundaries of the event with an
open alcoholic beverage container or an Entertainment District cup. All unfinished quantities of
alcohol and all District cups must be properly disposed of prior to the individual leaving the
event boundaries. Any person found with an Entertainment District cup or open container of
alcohol outside the set boundaries is subject to seizure by law enforcement or any officer of the
Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage Commission and the container and its contents shall be seized and
destroyed. In addition, any person found with a District container who is not displaying a proper

wristband shall have their container seized and the contents destroyed.

The seizure and destruction of the alcohol and any citation issued may be in addition to
law enforcement exercising their legal authority to charge or arrest any person for minor in
possession, public intoxication, disorderly conduct, or any other law that may be relevant to the
actions of the person. In addition, any person with a District container and/or wristband is subject
to age verification by law enforcement and/or any officer of the Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage

Commission while in the Entertainment District.
--- page 7 (OCR) ---
SECTION 11: Consumption of alcohol in a motor vehicle is prohibited. It shall be
unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage while in the confines of a motor
vehicle that is located upon any public street, parking lot, or other place in which the public has

or is permitted to have access within the Entertainment District.

SECTION 12: All other Arkansas laws including, but not limited to, Ark. Code Ann. § 3-
3-201, et seq (prohibited practices regarding alcoholic beverages), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71- 207
(disorderly conduct), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71-212 (public intoxication), Ark. Code Ann. § 5-71-

218 (consumption of alcohol in a motor vehicle) remain in effect and will be enforced.

SECTION 13: Nothing contained in this ordinance shall diminish the requirements or
authority of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division of the Department of Finance and

Administration concerning permits issued within the designated entertainment district.

SECTION 14: All Ordinances, Resolutions, or Orders of the City Council, or parts of

the same, in conflict with this Ordinance are repealed to the extent of such conflict.

SECTION 15: In addition to following all rules and regulations stated herein, a person
or entity seeking a permit hereunder must also comply with all federal laws, state laws, local
laws, and regulations and directives of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Division of the

Department of Finance and Administration.

SECTION 16: A violation of any part of these rules and regulations constitutes an
unclassified misdemeanor and may be punishable by a fine of $1,000 and/or a up to 10 days in

jail.
